pageSummary:
Background – Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company (MMWEC)
The Massachusetts Municipal Wholesale Electric Company (MMWEC) is the Commonwealth's designated joint‑action agency for municipal utilities. An article about a recent power‑purchase agreement notes that MMWEC is a not‑for‑profit, public corporation and political subdivision of Massachusetts created in 1975 to help municipal utilities collaborate for low‑cost, reliable and clean energyfirstlight.energy. MMWEC's statute allows the agency to issue tax‑exempt debt to finance energy facilities and enter agreements that reduce costs for member utilitiesfirstlight.energy. Beyond financing, MMWEC provides member utilities with power‑supply, financial and risk‑management services firstlight.energy. These services support 23 municipal light departments and help them meet clean‑energy mandates.

MMWEC also runs NextZero, an energy‑efficiency program for residential, commercial and industrial customers of participating municipal utilities. According to a program summary, NextZero offers home energy audits, appliance and lighting rebates, air‑conditioner and heat‑pump rebates and other incentives, with participating utilities tailoring the suite of rebates for their customersrebates.energy. Utilities may also offer battery‑storage rebatesrebates.energy. NextZero helps municipal utilities identify and implement energy‑efficiency projects and assists customers in lowering operating costs by incentivising energy‑efficiency measureswmgld.com.

Challenge
MMWEC's member utilities and energy‑efficiency programs generate large volumes of data, documents and customer interactions. Before this project, MMWEC lacked a modern platform for:

Member collaboration and reporting – utilities needed a secure way to access reports (market data, budgets, invoices, meeting notes) and submit required documents. Many processes were manual or email‑based, and sensitive reports had to be restricted by member town and access level.

Content and user management – MMWEC needed workflows for uploading board‑meeting notes, reports, marketing materials and newsletters while controlling who can view each item. Managing user roles (member, administrator, consultant, etc.) was a manual process.

Energy‑efficiency rebates – NextZero's rebate applications were paper‑based; customers had difficulty finding the right rebate forms for their municipal utility and there was no digital submission process. With new incentives such as battery‑storage rebatesrebates.energy, the program needed a modern web application.

Solution
MMWEC Member Portal
Working with MMWEC, we designed and implemented a secure, Drupal‑based member portal (webportal.mmwec.org). The portal provides a single entry point for MMWEC staff, municipal utilities and consultants. Key features include:

FeatureEvidence & description
Dynamic dashboardThe portal's landing page shows Day‑Ahead Locational Marginal Price charts and demand‑bid graphs (see screenshot below). Members can filter by town to see local demand bids and market prices, providing situational awareness.
Comprehensive navigationA persistent side menu gives access to Report Finder, Power Portfolio & Market Reports, Meter Data, NextZero resources, Budgets & Project Reports, Accounting Reports, Treasury Reports, Invoices & Billing Statements, Meetings & Newsletters and MMWEC organizational services. The design allows members to quickly locate the data they need without sifting through emails.
Board‑meeting notes workflowContent managers can add board‑meeting notes via Content > Add content > Board Meeting note and fill in title, date, meeting type, description, then upload agenda and meeting‑minutes files. They can set the scope of the notes so that only users with appropriate permissions see them.
Report Finder & manual PDF uploadThe system supports bulk and manual uploading of reports. For manual uploads, content managers navigate to Add content > PDF Document, supply a title, choose where it appears in the navigation, select member towns to limit visibility, upload the file and add an optional description. This process populates the Report Finder, enabling members to locate documents by type or town.
Marketing materials & social‑media assetsMarketing staff can add marketing material (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram posts, calendar events, flyers, videos and news releases) by choosing the asset type and filling in fields such as title, member town, date to post, optional image and user‑action checkbox. Users can mark items as completed, letting the marketing team know when content has been published.
Newsletters & announcementsThe portal includes a content type for newsletters and announcements. Staff enter a title, short description, publication date, newsletter type, file and optional image; the content then appears on a list‑view grid.
Granular user managementAuthorized administrators can create users via People > Add user. They populate email, username, password and select roles from Member, Member Admin, MMWEC Non‑admin, MMWEC Content Manager, API, Developer, MMWEC Admin and Administrator. Users are assigned to a member town and can have one or more document‑access levels, so they see only documents associated with their role and town. Additional fields allow publishing staff information to the staff directory or municipal manager phone list.

The combination of data dashboards, structured content types and granular permissions provides MMWEC with a scalable platform to support joint‑action activities. The portal improves transparency while maintaining strict control over sensitive documents.

NextZero Rebate Web Application
To support MMWEC's NextZero program, we built a responsive rebate web application (rebates.nextzero.org). The application aligns with MMWEC's mission of promoting energy efficiency and electrification. Features include:

  • Town‑specific rebate catalog – When a customer selects their municipal utility, the application displays a searchable catalog of available rebates. Categories such as Appliances, Lawn Equipment and Home Improvements help users find relevant incentives. Each rebate card lists the eligible technology (e.g., ENERGY STAR room air conditioner), rebate value (e.g., $40 for a room‑air conditioner) and an "Apply for Rebate" button.
  • Alignment with NextZero program – The application mirrors NextZero's offerings. Program summaries describe how NextZero provides home energy audits, appliance/lighting rebates, air‑conditioner and heat‑pump rebates and other incentives, with participating utilities tailoring the rebates for their customersrebates.energy. Rebates also support battery storage systemsrebates.energy.
  • Simplified application process – Applicants complete online forms rather than mailing paper documents. The portal collects user information, uploads necessary receipts and automatically routes submissions to the appropriate municipal utility. This digital workflow shortens processing times and reduces administrative burden.
  • Integration with member portal – Rebate analytics and application data feed into the member portal, allowing utilities to track rebate uptake alongside demand‑response programs. Marketing materials created in the portal link to specific rebates, ensuring consistent messaging across channels.

Impact & Outcomes

  • Centralised information hub – The member portal consolidates market data, reports, meetings, invoices and organizational services, giving MMWEC members a single source of truth. The board‑meeting note and report workflows ensure that sensitive documents are securely shared with the right audience.
  • Improved efficiency and governance – Manual processes such as uploading PDFs, managing marketing materials and creating newsletters are now standardised and tracked through the portal. Granular user roles and document access levels support governance and compliance.
  • Enhanced energy‑efficiency engagement – By digitising NextZero rebates, customers can easily find and apply for incentives, supporting MMWEC's goal of helping municipalities and residents reduce energy consumption and costsrebates.energywmgld.com. The integrated platform enables utilities to tailor rebates and track program success.

Summary
By designing and implementing both the MMWEC Member Portal and the NextZero Rebate Application, we provided MMWEC and its municipal utility members with modern digital infrastructure aligned with the agency's mission of delivering reliable, low‑cost and clean energy. The portal streamlines collaboration, reporting and content management, while the rebate application makes it easy for customers to participate in energy‑efficiency programs. Together, these solutions enhance MMWEC's ability to serve its members and accelerate Massachusetts' transition toward an efficient, low‑carbon electric system.
